title: Raining Fish
subtitle: What you need are sharp eyes to spot value, a touch of arcane skill, and a talking hat.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: So, I dreamt of eating a marshmallow last night, but it tasted like rubber! And the next day, my wife asked me why I ate the cotton she had in her nose.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: I said it's because the air was so dirty that I wanted to block up my throat. And she laughed.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: Of course, she says it might be better now that I can't shout and holler whenever someone scores.
A burst of static fills the air as the radio's owner changes the station.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: These are the highest level of professional arcanists! Their abilities lie far beyond the limits of our bodies, our perception, and everything else!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Arthur, mate, do you know what you're doing?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Go on then, be a little louder. May as well let everyone know a trusted servant of His Majesty's Government and his talking hat are hiding out in a pile of litter!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Oh, that's what you're worrying about? I guarantee you no person in their right mind will think that a brilliant mind such as yourself would decide to hide in a rubbish pile pretending to be a potato!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Ha-ha, since when did you become a comedian?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: I learned from the "best," mate. Once I'm back in Oz, I hope to be awarded the title of "Duke of Syd-knee-slapper."

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Not that anyone gives a toss about titles of nobility back home. We've got more important things to worry about in the red lands down under.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: You know, Brimley, old chap, you don't have to be a duke to be above people. All you need is someone tall enough to wear you on his head.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Bloody oath, mate! Like I'd let anyone pop me on their head. I'm an intelligent being, not a bloody accessory.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Shh!
A small monocular peeks out from among the garbage.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Look at that sailor over there. See the ropes in his hand? That right there is presently the most valuable material in all of London to me.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Right, a bit of rope, and what about it, mate?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: It's essential that I have it for my invention. We'll just wait for him to throw the ropes into the pile here, and then we'll be off, just as simple as that.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Come closer, closer. Ready now! He's nearly here!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: It's no longer useful to you, son. Just throw it down.
A bowl of freshly extracted fish guts is poured over him.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: BAAAH! *coughs*

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: *coughs* Mate, there's a lot of good that's come of being Awakened. I treasure all the adventures we've shared. But I'll tell you right now, I wouldn't have Awakened if I knew I'd end up in a rubbish bin covered in fish guts.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Just a little mistake. Just a LITTLE mistake.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: What are all these for exactly?
Mr. Fog gestures for Brimley to come closer, then, with a proud "whoosh," opens the large sack he's been filling over the last three days.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: These are my collections so far: a klaxon, a watering can, a fishbowl, and ...

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: A chamber pot?
Despite his lack of facial features, Mr. Fog can sense Brimley's disdain.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: You've gone full bonkers, mate! You're the Fogwalker! Aren't you ashamed of hiding in rubbish, stealing old junk?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: It's not junk, old chap. Every piece here will be invaluable to our work.
Mr. Fog's face hardens as he turns his gaze toward Brimley.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Each one is a necessary component for my invention.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Your invention?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: For ... Ahoy, sailor. You over there! Please wait!
Mr. Fog's attention is clearly still fixed on the sailor.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Would you mind terribly leaving us those old ropes you've got there!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Good lord, he's bound for the sanitarium at this rate.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Move along, move along! No pushing! Everyone will have their chance to vote for their favorite competitor!

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Oi, sweeny! You only pushed me out of the queue. Good bloody job, mate.

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: I'm voting for number 007! Mulson!

items.speaker: Neighbor II
items.text: Mulson, the first timer? Not on your life, mate! I'm down for 005 Bartley. She's the top seed!
The alley is full of stalls for the Uluru Qualifiers. A crowd of people is gathered, their faces painted with Uluru symbols in anticipation of the event.

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Three days to the qualifiers! Vote while you still can!

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Sir, oi, you over there with the black brolly, come on over, and vote for the winner!

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Oi, mister, stop your pushing!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: *panting* Oh, I'm terribly sorry, I ...

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Sorry, mate, we're on patrol!

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Sir, we have a situation over there.

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: Let's follow them.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcast
items.text: Now introducing the competitors for the Uluru London Qualifiers.

items.speaker: Will
items.text: Bartley, Bartley, Bartley!

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Oi! Who pushed me?

items.speaker: Neighbor II
items.text: Ouch! Mind your step, will you?

items.speaker: Neighbor I
items.text: Me? Was you that pushed me, weren't it! You should be the one minding your own feet!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Arthur, I think we're only making things worse trying to move through this crowd.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Looks like we've found our troublemakers. What do we do?

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: Keep up with them, and bring them in!

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Yes sir!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Arthur, next time, don't, don't get me involved. I think I'm feeling sick.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Haha, but he gave us the rope after all.
Mr. Fog grins as he looks at the small length of rope in his hand.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Stop right there!
He turns his head, and there, standing behind him, are two constables.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Seems you two rough sleepers are wanted in connection with a fight breaking out on Cross Street. I'll ask you to come quietly and cooperate.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Mate? Say something!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Wonderful! Now I have everything I need for my experiment! The properties of this sea-worn rope should be able to conduct the large particles into the purification vessels.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Mate, shut your gob for a minute and listen!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Yes, perfection! But how to measure and screen the size of the particles? We will need more sophisticated equipment. Huh? Why am I being handcuffed?

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Because you're being placed under arrest, sir.
The moment the two constables draw near, they freeze in place.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Wait a second.
Their eyes widen.

items.speaker: Police Constable I
items.text: Mr. Fog? Is that you?

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Bloody hell! Are you seriously telling me you recognized Fog before me! How many talking hats do you know?

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: Terribly sorry, gentlemen. I might not have recognized you through all this fog were it not for that iconic umbrella of yours.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Oh, naturally. Just as I've somehow failed to recognize the two ignoramuses that tried to handcuff a hat!
The shorter constable gives a series of subtle eye signals to the other.

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: We're sorry again, Mr. Fogwalker and Mr. Brimley.

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: But, we do need to ask you some questions, what with you running around disturbing the peace and nicking all these strange things you've got there.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Oh, I didn't steal anything! This is all just rubbish, and it's for official business. I'm going to lift the fog from London!
The two constables pause for a moment before their faces break into awkwardly sardonic smiles.

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: I see, I see. All just a terrible misunderstanding then!

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: Naturally, a bit of old rope, a car horn, unmistakably the latest in technology.

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: Anyways, mates. Best we let you go. You've got a city to save.

items.speaker: Police Constable II
items.text: We'll be off now.
With the handcuffs removed, Brimley takes a moment to stretch.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Glad that's over. I'm no fan of handcuffs, even if I don't have any hands.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: A little quiet, old chap. I'm just in the middle of a thought. How might I assemble it?

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: I-I'm sorry, mister, but I just heard what happened.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Huh?
Neither one of them had noticed the little girl who had appeared before them. She looks only half as old as Flutterpage.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Did you say "lifting the fog," mister? Are you really going to get rid of the big scary fog monster?
She blinks, her eyes bright and sparkling as she stares at Mr. Fog like a little goldfish in a tank.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Will that mean you can cure my mummy?

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: And bring back the blue sky?
Brimley glances at Mr. Fog.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Right?
When no one responds, the little girl grows anxious.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: And, and then, we can still have the Uluru Games, right?
Her eyes dart back and forth between Brimley and Mr. Fog, looking for any trace of comfort.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: My mummy said, if the fog keeps sticking around making people sick, then the games won't come.
A faint sob starts to creep into her voice.
Mr. Fog crouches down and shakes his sack of treasures, spreading them out on the ground.

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: Mate, this really isn't the time or place.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: A klaxon, a probe, a spoon, and a spool of weathered rope ...

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Assembled like so, perhaps using a large pot or a baby's bathtub ...
He furrows his brow, absorbed in the task at hand.
The girl gets on her knees as she leans in to get a closer look.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: It will still need a touch of the miraculous.
He gently blows into the base of the glass vessel.
There's a crackling sound as a few sparks of light flash briefly in the glass container.
Before long, a tiny, steady light is glowing within.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Voilà!

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: It's breathing!
The machine hums as it draws in air, filters it, and releases it through the other side.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: The Uluru Qualifiers will not just be fog-free, my little friend. They will be sunny.

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: But I'll need some help. Would you and your friends join me in this project, young lady?
The little girl's face blushes red.

items.speaker: Little Lisa
items.text: Y-Yes! I'll help. I'll ask my grandpa, my mummy, and Auntie Martha to help, too!

items.speaker: Mr. Fog
items.text: The more, the merrier! We're going to build the largest fog purification machine on earth—The London Air Pollution Auto-Detect Cleaner!

items.speaker: Brimley
items.text: That just looks like a great honking big vacuum to me, mate.
Old House, Cross Street

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Sulis, Sulis, all life's offerings I bring, as sacrifice to you, from the growing spring.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: The light will sprout within the world's egg lay.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Your endless quest brings parents' joyful day.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Parents' joyful day ...

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: What are you, a parrot?
After hanging in the upside-down pose of her ribbon dance for an hour, Willow finally decides to break the silence.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Fine, keep on then. Annoy an old woman to death if you like.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Another bad mood, eh, Ms. Willow? This one's your worst this week. I counted it up. Every 32 hours, steady as a clock, you start scoldin' me, scoldin' the plants, the ants, even flowers.

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: I thought we'd agreed—no more peeking round my house without permission.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Yeah, but you didn't kick me out, did you? And you gave me some rye bread and lemon jam. Don't quite know why you keep tryin' to act the big meanie, Ms. Willow. I know you're a softie, now—deep down.
*rrrrip—* The ribbon suspending Willow finally gives way, sending her quickly to the ground.
She hits the floor with a heavy thud.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Ms. Willow!

items.speaker: Willow
items.text: Ouch! Ah, it hurts.
Are you practicing for the qualifiers?
A distant voice reaches her.
The corner of Willow's mouth twitches.

items.speaker: Flutterpage
items.text: Hello again, Ms. Swan.
A blonde woman stands on the other side of the garden fence, her face half-covered by the curled stems of a carnivorous plant.
